predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Only eight episodes with a crossover team-up structure that moves fast — the shortest and most plot-driven entry in the Netflix-Marvel run. Weak Hand storyline caps the pull, but the low commitment makes it easy to clear.

title: Operation Buffalo
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Short Australian period limited series, but its tonal mix of nuclear-testing satire and drama is uneven, and the pacing is discursive rather than driving. Steady watching, no strong pull to the next episode.

title: Watchmen
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Nine episodes of dense mythology with real jaw-drop reveals — high sustain in your Dark cluster. Docked one because early episodes are deliberately cryptic, so the hook takes two or three episodes to bite.

title: See

title: Twin Peaks
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 2/5: Deliberately dreamlike and digressive, with a notorious mid-S2 collapse and a Return season that is actively anti-narrative. Its own prediction stacks experimental and slow penalties — a show to study, not to be pulled through.

title: Money Heist
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: A heist in progress with a cliffhanger ending nearly every episode — one of the most aggressively bingeable structures ever made. The known later-parts fizzle is a quality problem, not a momentum one; subtitles are the only real friction.

title: Maid
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: A ten-episode escape narrative with constant setbacks generates real 'will she get out' propulsion, and Little Fires Everywhere (your binge 5) is the adjacent shape. Grinding poverty and repeated cruelty cap it at 4 for consecutive viewing.

title: The Kominsky Method
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Gentle half-hour comfort comedy with witty dialogue and very likeable leads — the frictionless easy-watch register, closest to Shrinking at your binge 4. Low stakes and no plot engine keep it off 5.

title: Smoke
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Arson investigation with a serialised hunt across a short complete run — a case engine with a genuine spine. Soft audience reception (49%) suggests the execution may not fully deliver on that structure.

title: Amazing Stories
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Standalone anthology episodes with no connecting thread, and reviews call the entries forgettable (41% critics). Easy to sample, nothing to continue — anthologies without a frame reset momentum every time.

title: Inventing Anna
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: A con unravelling is a propulsive true-crime shape and Garner's performance carries it, but its own prediction flags the nine-episode runtime as stretched — the padding is what keeps it off 5.

title: We Were the Lucky Ones
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: WWII family-survival story cross-cutting between separated siblings, which builds natural 'what happened to them' momentum. Heavy subject matter caps consecutive viewing — the same ceiling as your other WWII together watches rather than a soap-tier 5.

title: Ozark
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Cliffhanger-driven crime escalation across four complete seasons, engineered for continuation. Kept off 5 by relentless bleakness — the grim tone caps how many you want consecutively, the same ceiling that holds Breaking Bad at 4 rather than a comfort-tier 5.

title: Five Days at Memorial
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Eight episodes, but the back half turns into an investigative inquiry after the hurricane crisis resolves, which drains urgency. Harrowing medical-triage content makes consecutive episodes hard going — high purpose, low compulsion.

title: Euphoria
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Visually hypnotic with real melodramatic pull, but structurally episodic character portraits and relentlessly bleak addiction content make consecutive viewing heavy. Style-forward rather than plot-driven.

title: Rectify
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 2/5: Famously the slowest prestige drama of its era — long silences, interior stillness, almost no plot velocity, across four seasons. Its own prediction stacks slow-burn and dark-without-hope penalties. Genuinely hard to keep going.

title: Rosehaven
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Gentle low-stakes Australian character comedy with no plot engine, across five seasons of short episodes. Easy to watch but nothing pulls you forward — closest to your Fisk score of 3, the same deadpan Australian comedy register.

title: Echo 3
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: A hostage-rescue premise should drive hard, but reviews call it overlong 'dad television' that delivers action while falling short on character across ten episodes. Stretched pacing blunts the hook.

title: The Witcher
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: S1's scrambled non-linear timelines are actively confusing, which its own prediction flags, and the early structure is monster-of-the-week. Recasting mid-run breaks investment further. Some action pull, weak coherence.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Seven seasons of largely standalone episodes with wildly variable early quality — the multi-episode arcs are excellent but scattered through a 130-episode back catalogue. That cold-start bulk is the abandonment shape, franchise pull notwithstanding.

title: KEVIN CAN F**K HIMSELF
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: The tonal whiplash between garish multi-cam and bleak drama is deliberately jarring, which works against easy consecutive viewing. An escape plot gives some spine, but its own prediction notes the concept is sharper than the execution sustains.

title: Yellowjackets
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: A dual-timeline question engine is the strongest hook shape in your data, and I previously waved the drag off as a quality worry. title: Modern Love Tokyo
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Standalone anthology romance — every episode resets, so there is no forward pull by design. Very low commitment and easy to dip into, which is its appeal, but structurally the opposite of a binge engine.

title: Star Trek: Prodigy
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Serialised kids' Trek with a continuous quest arc and short episodes, and the franchise hook is real for you (Lower Decks 5, Discovery, Strange New Worlds 4). YA pitch keeps it below the top tier.

title: Atlanta
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Loosely connected surreal vignettes with standalone bottle episodes and little forward plot — deliberately anti-serial. Short episodes make it easy, but the experimental structure gives no momentum.

title: The Sopranos
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: The founding prestige-antihero show, built on episodic vignettes and psychotherapy rather than serialised cliffhangers, across six seasons. This is the class where your own scores sit at 3 (Better Call Saul, Veep) — craft over compulsion.

title: Wellington Paranormal
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Case-of-the-week deadpan mockumentary in very short episodes — frictionless to start, but its own prediction calls it thin and repetitive across a full run. Funny in bursts, no forward pull.

title: Peaky Blinders
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Tight six-episode seasons with a clear antagonist arc each series, so momentum is high and commitment per season is low. Stylised, occasionally repetitive plotting across six seasons keeps it below 5.

title: Mr. Robot
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Puzzle-box with unreliable-narrator reveals gives it high sustain — the Dark shape, which you scored 4 for exactly this reason. Dense, stylised early episodes slow the hook before the first big twist lands, so the front end asks for patience the back end repays.

title: Roseanne
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Classic multi-cam family sitcom — self-contained episodes, no serialisation, and ten seasons of cold-start back catalogue. Easy comfort viewing in bursts, but nothing pulls forward and late seasons are uneven.

title: Boardwalk Empire
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Stately Sopranos-lineage period crime — lavish and slow, built on political manoeuvring rather than cliffhangers, across five seasons. This is the prestige-heavy class where your own scores cluster at 3 (Better Call Saul, Boardwalk's closest tonal relative).

title: Task

title: Dune: Prophecy
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Six episodes but dense Bene Gesserit politics and heavy exposition dominate over plot momentum — its own prediction notes it is more political drama than action. Handsome and slow-moving.

title: Bookish

title: The Penguin
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Eight-episode gangster rise with betrayals landing at episode ends, so it moves. Grimy, oppressive noir atmosphere caps consecutive viewing — the same bleakness ceiling that holds Ozark and Breaking Bad at 4.

title: Band of Brothers

title: Succession

predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Game of Thrones political intrigue with strong episode-end escalations and a civil war building. Held at 4 by the multi-year time jumps and recasting in S1, which repeatedly reset investment and interrupted momentum.

predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Reviews specifically cite pacing problems and thin characterisation, and the structure is mission-of-the-week air combat with a rotating cast — episodic repetition rather than accumulating pull. Notably weaker on this axis than Band of Brothers.

title: Chief of War

title: Lioness

title: The Beast in Me
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Eight-episode cat-and-mouse psychological thriller with a did-he-do-it hook, which is strong pull, and a short closed run. Character-study pacing over thriller velocity keeps it a notch below the pure whodunits at 5.

title: Wednesday
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Its own prediction already calls it bingeable — a YA mystery with a season-long whodunit, cliffhanger episode endings and short seasons. Closed-question mystery plus light tone is the top-scoring shape in your data.

title: The Peripheral
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Gibson mystery-box with VR-future reveals and episode-end hooks — genuinely propulsive sci-fi. Cancelled on a cliffhanger means the payoff never lands, which is what caps the rating rather than the momentum.

title: True Detective
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: S1's dual-timeline investigation is a strong mystery engine with mounting dread. The philosophical monologues and deliberate Louisiana languor slow it below a pure page-turner, and the anthology format means momentum resets after eight episodes.

title: Apple Cider Vinegar
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Six-episode fraud unravelling with a cultural-moment engine — the propulsive true-crime shape that works for you (The Dropout, Quiz). Unlikeable subject and a smug narrative register add friction, so 4 not 5.
